claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active imperatives and verbs drive many sentences ('Act singly,' 'Be it how it will,' 'do right now,' 'They shed,' 'He is attended'), but abstract nominalizations also carry significant weight ('conformity,' 'consciousness,' 'majesty,' 'pedigree,' 'virtue'). Neither mode fully dominates.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Short declarative sentences coordinate paratactically ('The force of character is cumulative. All the foregone days of virtue work their health into this.'), but subordinate constructions also appear ('because it is not of to-day,' 'which so fills the imagination,' 'so they be each honest'). The passage alternates between both modes.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication immediately and trail qualifications afterward — 'Your genuine action will explain itself, and will explain your other genuine actions' — with the notable exception of the rhetorical question answered by a suspended fragment ('The consciousness of a train of great days and victories behind').
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is intensely performable — imperative commands ('Act singly,' 'Always scorn appearances,' 'do right now'), rhetorical questions, and the climactic tricolon ('throws thunder into Chatham's voice, and dignity into Washington's port, and America into Adams's eye') all demand vocal emphasis, dynamic range, and a preacher's cadence.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Plain Anglo-Saxon imperatives and monosyllables ('do right now,' 'Act singly') coexist with elevated Latinate abstractions ('ephemeris,' 'immaculate pedigree,' 'cumulative,' 'harmonious'), producing the characteristic Emersonian blend of oracular plainness and philosophical elevation.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose foregrounds its own surface through deliberate rhetorical figures: the tricolon climax on Chatham/Washington/Adams, the anaphoric 'because it is not' repetitions, the aphoristic compression of sentences like 'Greatness appeals to the future,' and the extended metaphor of the zigzag ship — all draw attention to the language as crafted performance.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry biographical events — 'was born,' 'was placed,' 'wore,' 'delighted,' 'said' — but nominal constructions also appear in the middle section: 'in a relation of patron and client,' 'in hostility to Richard,' 'in helping his young client forward.' Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between event-driven narration and nominal summary.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The Cardinal Morton sentence chains coordinate clauses with 'and' and semicolons in a paratactic sequence ('had been... was busy... was a chief adviser... who made him... and nine months afterwards'), while other sentences embed subordinate material through 'as,' 'for,' 'whoever,' and relative clauses — producing a genuine mixture of both modes.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and trail qualifications afterward — 'Sir Thomas More... was born in 1478, in Milk Street, in the city of London' — with appositives and elaborations following the main verb. The parenthetical dash construction ('of talk at whose table there are recollections in Utopia') is the one notable periodic interruption.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has some performable moments — the direct quotation at the close and the rhythmic list of Morton's career — but the middle section's explanatory generalizing ('It was not unusual for persons of wealth or influence') flattens into an unvoiced, expository register that resists emphasis.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is neither strikingly Latinate nor plainly Anglo-Saxon — words like 'household,' 'livery,' 'patron,' 'client,' 'hostility,' and 'influence' sit in an unmarked middle register appropriate to Victorian biographical prose.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is entirely instrumental, moving the reader through biographical facts without calling attention to its own surface. The one structural flourish — the inverted relative clause in dashes around the Utopia reference — is a minor exception that does not disturb the overall transparency.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage mixes nominal constructions ('editorship,' 'publication,' 'translation,' 'defence') with active verbs carrying human agents ('was sent,' 'went,' 'was written,' 'had conducted,' 'attended,' 'vindicated'). Neither mode dominates; the biographical catalogue form requires both naming and action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between hypotactic relative clauses ('of which the second,' 'that caused More to write') and paratactic coordinate chains, especially in the Burnet sentence where actions are strung together with 'and' — 'conducted... attended... vindicated... been deprived.'
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and trail qualifications, dates, and elaborations afterward — 'The book was first printed at Louvain, late in 1516, under the editorship of...' The one exception is the long Burnet sentence, which accumulates subordinate actions before its concluding point.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is largely flat and enumerative — a scholarly chronicle — but the Burnet sentence builds genuine rhetorical momentum through its accumulation of actions, and the final two sentences carry a quiet editorial voice with performable emphasis ('the same sense of unreason in high places').
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is educated but not heavily Latinate; it sits in a plain scholarly register — 'companionship,' 'introductory,' 'editorship' are Latinate but unremarkable, while the syntax and vocabulary remain accessible and unmarked throughout.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is entirely instrumental — a bibliographic and biographical record — with no sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or self-conscious structural display. The language is a window onto facts, not a surface calling attention to itself.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage mixes active verbs with human agents ('he spoke,' 'he discovered,' 'he depended,' 'he had practised') alongside nominal constructions ('execution of justice,' 'presence of mind,' 'commendation of the severe execution'). Neither mode dominates; the character portrait sections are more verbal, the evaluative passages more nominal.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'which,' 'when,' 'that,' 'as,' 'though,' and 'having' constructions, creating layered subordination — 'by that he discovered their spirit and presence of mind; with which he was much delighted when it did not grow up to impudence, as bearing a great resemblance.' The passage sustains multiple levels of qualification throughout.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Main predications arrive early and qualifications trail behind in coordinate and subordinate chains — 'he was of a middle stature, not broken with age; his looks begot reverence rather than fear.' The long sentence about Morton's wisdom follows the same pattern: main clause first, elaborations appended.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is explicitly framed as oral narration ('said he,' 'Mr. More knows well what he was') and carries natural emphases and rhythmic pauses suited to performance. The embedded direct speech of the lawyer ('who were then hanged so fast that there were sometimes twenty on one gibbet!') adds dramatic vocal range.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction blends Latinate terms ('venerable,' 'conversation,' 'prodigious,' 'traverses of fortune') with plain Anglo-Saxon constructions ('his looks begot reverence,' 'he spoke both gracefully and weightily'), producing a cultivated but accessible middle register characteristic of humanist prose translation.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its character-portrait function, but the rhythmic tricolon patterning ('wisdom and virtues,' 'easy, but serious and grave,' 'gracefully and weightily,' 'understanding, and a prodigious memory') draws mild attention to its own rhetorical surface as deliberate encomium structure.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry the dialogue forward — 'answered,' 'think,' 'propose,' 'become,' 'hearken,' 'found' — but the argumentative passages lean on nominalizations and abstractions: 'relation,' 'aversion,' 'counsels,' 'design,' 'happiness,' 'notions.' Neither mode dominates; the conversational frame pulls toward verbs while the philosophical content pulls toward nouns.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are deeply embedded through 'that,' 'if,' 'which,' 'because,' and 'while' constructions, often stacked several levels deep — 'I still think that if you could overcome that aversion which you have to the courts of princes, you might, by the advice which it is in your power to give, do a great deal of good.' The syntax is architecturally subordinating throughout.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Some sentences are running, delivering their main predication early and trailing qualifications ('They are not so base-minded but that they would willingly do it'); others are periodic, suspending the main clause behind conditional and relative material ('except kings themselves became philosophers, they who from their childhood are corrupted with false notions would never fall in entirely'). The two modes alternate across the passage.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person address and dialogue frame create natural performable moments — the turn-taking between speakers, the rhetorical pivot of 'It is no wonder if' — but the long embedded clauses flatten the rhythm and resist sustained vocal emphasis, producing a prose that is speakable but not oratorically charged.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is consistently formal and Latinate: 'relation,' 'aversion,' 'counsels,' 'corrupted,' 'philosophers,' 'design,' 'notions.' The register is that of humanist philosophical dialogue — elevated but not ceremonial, sustained throughout without colloquial breaks.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws no attention to its own surface — no sound patterns, no rhetorical figures on display, no self-conscious structural performance. The elaborate syntax serves the argument without foregrounding itself; the language is entirely instrumental, pointing through to the ideas about philosophers and kings.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry much of the descriptive work — 'comes in,' 'spreads itself,' 'appears above water,' 'conquered,' 'designed to separate' — but nominal constructions also appear in clusters: 'the entry into the bay,' 'great convenience for mutual commerce,' 'that measure of politeness.' Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between verb-driven geography and noun-anchored abstraction.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage moves between both modes: short coordinate chains ('the whole coast is, as it were, one continued harbour') sit alongside embedded subordinate constructions ('so that if any stranger should enter into the bay without one of their pilots he would run great danger'). The conditional and relative clauses create hypotactic depth, but many sentences simply add observations in sequence.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and trail qualifications afterward — 'Its figure is not unlike a crescent,' 'The channel is known only to the natives; so that...' The one periodic gesture ('if some marks that are on the coast did not direct their way; and if these should be but a little shifted, any fleet... would be certainly lost') is notable precisely because it is exceptional in this otherwise front-loaded prose.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has a measured, cartographic evenness for most of its length, but the final sentences — 'Utopus, that conquered it (whose name it still carries, for Abraxa was its first name)' — introduce a narrative warmth and ironic parenthetical that invites vocal performance. The conditional passage about the fleet being 'certainly lost' also carries rhetorical emphasis.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is neither aggressively Latinate nor plainly Anglo-Saxon — words like 'environed,' 'politeness,' 'uncivilised,' and 'continent' sit alongside 'rocks,' 'sea,' 'bay,' 'tower,' and 'coast.' This is the unmarked middle register of early modern English prose translation, functional and clear without being either elevated or colloquial.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws no attention to its own surface — no sound patterns, no rhetorical figures on display, no meta-linguistic gestures. The parenthetical '(whose name it still carries, for Abraxa was its first name)' is the closest thing to self-conscious structural play, but even this serves the content rather than advertising the writing.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real weight — 'shaking and squinting,' 'sold readily,' 'lie on the shelf,' 'hit only what they aim at' — but nominalizations and noun-heavy constructions also appear: 'the condition of the operatives,' 'the principal object,' 'the lapse of a season.' Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between concrete verbal action and abstract nominal framing.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Hypotactic embedding appears in the long conditional and relative clause chains ('since, as far as I have heard or observed, the principal object is, not that... but...'), but the passage also contains strongly paratactic moments — 'In the long run men hit only what they aim at. Therefore, though they should fail immediately, they had better aim at something high' — where short declarative sentences stand in coordinate relation.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence is periodic, suspending its main clause behind a long fronted subject and participial phrase; but many sentences run forward immediately — 'The manufacturers have learned,' 'It is not barbarous merely because,' 'I cannot believe' — delivering their predications early and trailing qualifications afterward.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person intrusions ('I cannot believe,' 'as far as I have heard or observed') and the aphoristic closing sentences ('In the long run men hit only what they aim at') carry a distinct, performable personality — sardonic, morally pointed, capable of rising to emphasis. The prose invites vocal stress and dynamic range.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction moves between plain Anglo-Saxon concreteness ('threads,' 'shelf,' 'skin-deep,' 'clad') and moderate Latinate abstraction ('comparatively,' 'unalterable,' 'corporations,' 'operatives'), settling into an unmarked middle register characteristic of the familiar essay rather than either high academic or low colloquial prose.
claude_justifications.opacity: Several moments draw attention to the prose surface — the unexpected analogy of tattooing, the chiastic logic of 'not that mankind may be well and honestly clad, but that corporations may be enriched,' and the epigrammatic compression of the closing aphorism — but much of the passage is instrumentally transparent, moving through its argument without foregrounding its own language.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs drive the prose throughout — 'think,' 'buy,' 'go round,' 'look,' 'please,' 'brag,' 'wake' — with human agents performing concrete actions. Nominalizations are sparse; even abstract intentions ('to brag,' 'to wake') are cast as infinitive actions rather than noun-forms.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The Cato quotation runs in paratactic coordinate chains ('turn it thus... not to buy greedily; nor spare your pains... and do not think'), while Thoreau's own sentences layer subordinate clauses ('if it is good,' 'that it may please me,' 'if only to wake my neighbors up'), creating a blend of both modes.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Main predications arrive early and qualifications trail behind — 'I think I shall not buy greedily, but go round and round it as long as I live, and be buried in it first, that it may please me the more at last.' The final sentence builds toward its punchline ('if only to wake my neighbors up') but the main clause still arrives before the conditional.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is saturated with first-person personality — the wry aside about the bad translation, the self-deprecating humor of being buried in the farm, the crowing chanticleer image. Natural emphases and tonal shifts (scholarly, ironic, boastful) make this highly performable.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The passage moves fluidly between registers: the scholarly citation of Latin Cato and the word 'lustily' sit alongside plain Anglo-Saxon diction ('go round,' 'look at it,' 'wake my neighbors up'), producing a characteristically Thoreauvian blend of learned and vernacular.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws attention to its own surface through the chanticleer figure (a deliberate rhetorical flourish), the meta-linguistic gesture about the bad translation, and the self-conscious echo of 'go round and round' — the writing performs its own wit rather than simply delivering information.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is driven by active verbs with a human agent throughout — cut, pared, felled, greeted, suspended, peeled, rolled, chewed, laughed, tumbled, rolled, exclaimed, warmed, sat, alight, pecked. Nominalizations are rare and incidental; the prose moves through physical actions observed in sequence.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage blends both modes: long coordinate chains of 'and' connect actions within sentences (paratactic), while subordinate clauses introduced by 'which,' 'that,' 'when,' 'though,' and 'as' embed qualifications and conditions (hypotactic). Neither fully dominates, though the paratactic 'and' chains are the more characteristic feature.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Main predications arrive early and observations trail afterward in coordinate chains — 'He cut his trees level and close to the ground, that the sprouts which came up afterward might be more vigorous.' The one near-periodic construction ('Such an exuberance of animal spirits had he') is an exception that proves the rule.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose invites performance — the direct quotation ('By George! I can enjoy myself well enough here chopping'), the italicized dialect ('fellers'), and the rhythmic accumulation of physical detail all create natural emphases and tonal shifts between the narrator's dry observation and the woodchopper's exuberance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is predominantly plain Anglo-Saxon — chopper, stumps, bark, log, kettle, fingers, fellers — with almost no Latinate vocabulary except occasional words like 'inexpressible,' 'salutation,' and 'exuberance,' which stand out precisely because the surrounding register is so plain.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its physical observation, letting the woodchopper's actions speak without calling attention to the language itself; but the deliberate structural display of the 'and' chains, the italicized dialect, and the rhetorical inversion ('Such an exuberance of animal spirits had he') create moments where the writing surface becomes briefly visible.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The prose is dense with nominalizations and abstract nouns — 'representation,' 'cognition,' 'intuition,' 'conception,' 'consciousness,' 'necessity,' 'perception,' 'capacity' — chained through prepositional phrases. Verbs are largely copular ('must be,' 'is,' 'can be') rather than action-driving.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are deeply embedded through 'which,' 'that,' 'in order that,' 'in so far as,' 'consequently,' and participial constructions, creating multiple ranked levels of subordination within single sentences.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates strategies: some sentences open with the main predication and trail qualifications (running), while others — especially the long final sentence — front-load conditional and qualifying material before resolving ('Now, how can... exist... Obviously not otherwise than in so far as...'), producing a periodic effect.
claude_justifications.voice: The rhetorical questions ('What, then, must be...?', 'Now, how can...?') and the emphatic 'Obviously' create moments of performable emphasis and dialectical energy, but the surrounding abstract nominalization flattens the dynamic range and resists sustained vocal performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Consistently formal and Latinate throughout: 'apodeictic,' 'anterior,' 'empirical,' 'synthetically,' 'à priori,' 'cognition.' No Anglo-Saxon plainness intrudes; the diction is technical-philosophical throughout.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in Lanham's sense — it aims to deliver argument rather than display its own surface — but the parenthetical cross-references '(Introd. V.)' and '(Introd. II.)' and the italicized technical terms ('apodeictic,' 'à priori') draw momentary attention to the text as a constructed, self-referential object.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is saturated with nominalizations and abstract nouns: determination, existence, phenomena, succession, simultaneity, perception, unity, validity. Verbs are almost entirely copular or weakly transitive ('are,' 'is considered,' 'can receive,' 'determines'), serving mainly to link noun-chains rather than drive action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are deeply embedded through 'that,' 'which,' 'inasmuch as,' 'as regards,' and participial constructions, creating multiple ranked levels of subordination. The passage builds hierarchical qualification upon qualification rather than coordinating in parallel chains.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Some sentences open with front-loaded qualifications that suspend the main predication ('for this is impossible, inasmuch as...'), while others deliver their main clause early and trail elaborations afterward ('time is not considered as that in which...'). Neither pattern dominates consistently.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is almost entirely unperformable — abstract, impersonal, and without natural emphatic peaks or dynamic range. There is no speaker behind the statement, only a logical apparatus; attempting vocal performance would feel absurd.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Heavily Latinate and technical throughout: 'synthetical unity,' 'dynamical,' 'phenomena,' 'simultaneity,' 'à priori.' The diction is philosophical-technical, the highest and most specialized register.
claude_justifications.opacity: Despite its extreme difficulty, the prose makes no self-conscious display of its own surface — no sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or structural performance. The language is purely instrumental, attempting to point through itself to logical content, however opaque that content may be conceptually.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The prose is almost entirely driven by abstract nominalizations — understanding, production, unity, phenomena, reason, principles, cognition, conception — chained through prepositional phrases ('for the production of unity of phenomena by virtue of rules'). The few verbs present ('applies,' 'gives,' 'called') are weak copulas or near-copulas serving to link noun clusters rather than to drive action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are embedded through 'which,' 'by means of,' 'in so far as,' and participial constructions, creating multiple levels of subordination. The second sentence in particular layers three relative clauses inside each other before resolving.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage mixes both tendencies: the opening definitional sentences deliver their main predications early and trail qualifications (running), while the long second sentence suspends resolution through embedded relative clauses and appositives before arriving at the final qualification about the nature of rational unity (periodic).
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is almost entirely resistant to vocal performance — there are no natural emphases, no dynamic range, no personality behind the statement. The flat, definitional evenness of 'the understanding is a faculty for the production of' makes any attempt at expressive reading feel absurd.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Exclusively Latinate and technical philosophical diction throughout: 'faculty,' 'phenomena,' 'sensuous,' 'cognition,' 'conceptions,' 'à priori,' 'rational unity.' No Anglo-Saxon plainness anywhere in the passage.
claude_justifications.opacity: Despite the extreme abstraction and syntactic density, the prose draws no attention to its own surface — there are no sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or self-conscious structural display. The language is purely instrumental, serving the conceptual argument without foregrounding itself as language.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is dense with nominalizations and abstract nouns: 'phenomenon,' 'antithetic,' 'sophistry,' 'conviction,' 'illusion,' 'scepticism,' 'confidence,' 'persistence,' 'euthanasia.' The verbs ('meets,' 'falls,' 'compelled') are relatively few and often passive or copular, with the conceptual weight carried by noun phrases chained through prepositions.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are deeply embedded through 'which,' 'that,' and participial constructions — 'which does not require to be sought for,' 'which a merely one-sided illusion produces,' 'without granting a fair hearing.' Multiple levels of subordination stack inside each sentence, creating a ranked hierarchical structure.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The main predications are repeatedly delayed behind qualifying and subordinate material — 'For here a new phenomenon... meets us — a perfectly natural antithetic, which does not require..., but into which reason of itself unavoidably falls.' The reader must hold suspended elements before the resolution arrives, and the final sentence withholds its punch ('euthanasia of pure reason') until the end.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has some performable moments — the antithetical structure of 'either... or' and the rhetorical climax of 'euthanasia of pure reason' invite emphasis and dynamic range. However, the density of abstraction and the parenthetical interruptions ('to be sure,' 'on the one hand... on the other') create friction against smooth oral delivery.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Heavily Latinate and philosophical throughout: 'antithetic,' 'sophistry,' 'scepticism,' 'dogmatical,' 'euthanasia,' 'unavoidably.' The diction is consistently formal and technical, characteristic of translated German Enlightenment philosophical prose.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in that it serves its philosophical argument instrumentally, but the deliberate antithetical structure ('either... or,' 'on the one hand... on the other') and the conspicuous rhetorical flourish of 'euthanasia of pure reason' draw momentary attention to the surface as a formal display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nominalizations are present throughout — 'design,' 'approbation,' 'judgment,' 'examination,' 'instruction' — but first-person active verbs also carry real weight: 'I have planned,' 'I was willing,' 'I shall proceed,' 'I consider,' 'am determined.' Neither mode fully dominates the other.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage mixes both modes: hypotactic subordination appears in 'that all the subjects I have there planned,' 'in order to try,' and 'whatever it be,' while the final sentence coordinates two independent clauses with 'but,' and several sentences simply run in sequence without embedding.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences are running — 'The subjects of the Understanding and Passions make a compleat chain' delivers its predication immediately — but the conditional 'If I have the good fortune to meet with success, I shall proceed' is a clean periodic construction, and the final sentence suspends its second clause behind a qualifying phrase.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person address and the direct appeal to the public give the prose a performable quality — there are natural emphases on 'compleat chain,' 'greatest reward,' and 'best instruction' — but the even, measured tone and abstract diction keep it from strong vocal performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Latinate diction predominates: 'approbation,' 'examination,' 'compleat,' 'determination,' 'instruction,' 'Treatise.' The register is formal and philosophical throughout, consistent with eighteenth-century learned prose.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws no attention to its own surface — no sound patterns, no rhetorical figures, no structural display. The language is entirely instrumental, serving the author's announcement of his project and his deference to public judgment.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real argumentative weight — 'exist,' 'pretend,' 'draw,' 'prove,' 'examines' — but the passage also relies on nominal constructions like 'the composition of extension by indivisible points,' 'the objects of geometry,' and 'proportions and positions.' Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between definitional noun-chains and active predication.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Hypotactic embedding appears in the relative clauses ('whose proportions and positions it examines,' 'that they are impossible') and subordinating conjunctions ('upon any other supposition than that of'), but the passage also uses strongly paratactic parallel structures — 'They never did exist; for… They never can exist; for…' — creating a deliberate rhetorical balance between the two modes.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Some sentences are running — 'It is evident that all this is perfectly unintelligible upon any other supposition…' delivers its main claim early and trails qualifications. Others are more periodic, front-loading conditions before resolution, as in 'How else could any thing exist without length, without breadth, or without depth?' which suspends its rhetorical force through accumulation.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is clearly performable — the rhetorical question 'How else could any thing exist…?', the first-person intrusion 'I find,' 'in my opinion,' and the parallel anaphora 'They never did exist… They never can exist' all create natural emphases and dynamic range. A speaker could easily stress and vary these sentences.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is neither ceremonially Latinate nor plainly Anglo-Saxon — terms like 'indivisible,' 'composition,' 'demonstrations,' and 'conformable' are Latinate, but the syntax and vocabulary are largely accessible and unmarked, characteristic of eighteenth-century philosophical prose aimed at an educated general reader.
claude_justifications.opacity: The passage is largely transparent in that the language serves the argument, but the deliberate anaphoric parallelism — 'They never did exist; for… They never can exist; for…' — and the triadic accumulation 'without length, without breadth, or without depth' draw mild attention to the prose surface as a rhetorical construction rather than pure conceptual vehicle.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nominalizations dominate — belief, assent, vivacity, perception, impression, repetition, foundation, inference, survey, penetration, dependance, existence, impossibility, contradiction — chained through prepositional phrases. Verbs are largely copular ('is,' 'appears') or weak ('attends,' 'constitutes,' 'lays'), with the nouns carrying the conceptual weight.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'which,' 'that,' 'when,' 'if,' and 'as' constructions, creating layered subordination — 'the belief or assent, which always attends the memory and senses, is nothing but the vivacity of those perceptions they present; and that this alone distinguishes them.' Coordination exists but serves to link hypotactic units rather than replace them.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage mixes both patterns: some sentences open with front-loaded conditionals or participial phrases that delay the main clause ('When we pass from a present impression...,' 'In tracing this relation...'), while others deliver their predication early and trail qualifications ('There is no object, which implies the existence of any other if...').
claude_justifications.voice: The philosophical 'we' and the argumentative structure ('It is easy to observe,' 'But as all distinct ideas are separable') create a mild rhetorical presence and some natural emphatic stress, but the abstract diction and even pacing resist strong vocal performance — there is a measured, lecturing quality rather than oratorical dynamism.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate and formal throughout: 'vivacity,' 'perception,' 'penetration,' 'dependance,' 'inference,' 'contradiction,' 'impossibility.' The diction is consistently philosophical and elevated, with almost no Anglo-Saxon plainness.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is instrumental — it serves its philosophical argument without calling attention to its own surface through sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or structural display. The language is a vehicle for the epistemological analysis, not an object of attention in itself.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nouns dominate the conceptual load — cause, effect, gravity, belief, connexion, conjunction, variation, diminution — chained through prepositional phrases ('of a number of parts,' 'of the several effects,' 'of a proportionable part'). Verbs are largely copular or weakly transitive ('is,' 'arises,' 'contains,' 'proves'), serving mainly to link nominal constructions rather than drive action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are embedded through 'because,' 'that,' 'which,' and 'according to' constructions, creating layered subordination. The passage builds logical hierarchies — premise, sub-clause, qualification — rather than coordinating assertions in parallel chains.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage mixes both patterns: some sentences open with subordinate conditionals or causal clauses that delay the main predication ('As the belief which we have of any event, encreases or diminishes according to the number of chances or past experiments, it is to be considered...'), while others deliver their main assertion early and trail elaboration ('This connexion or constant conjunction sufficiently proves the one part to be the cause of the other').
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person plural 'we' and the rhetorical structure of demonstration ('Thus, because...we conclude') give the prose a lecturing presence that is performable, with natural emphases on logical pivots. However, the density of abstract nominal constructions flattens the dynamic range and resists full vocal animation.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'phaenomena,' 'compounded,' 'proportionable,' 'connexion,' 'conjunction,' 'diminution.' The register is that of eighteenth-century philosophical discourse — elevated, technical, and ceremonial.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is entirely instrumental — it exists to convey a logical argument about causation and compound effects, and draws no attention to its own surface through sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or structural display. The numbered 'Thirdly' signals a treatise structure, but this is organizational rather than self-conscious stylistic performance.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry significant weight — 'paint,' 'select,' 'place,' 'direct,' 'excite,' 'regulate,' 'make us feel' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns are also prominent: 'entertainment, instruction, and reformation,' 'the science of human nature,' 'the love of probity and true honour.' Neither mode dominates; the prose moves between conceptual abstraction and enacted action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between hypotactic embedding ('as influenced in his measures by taste and sentiment; pursuing one object, and avoiding another, according to the value which these objects seem to possess') and paratactic enumeration ('They select... place... direct... make us feel... excite and regulate'). The catalogue of philosopher-actions in the final sentences is strongly paratactic, while the earlier characterizations are hypotactic.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Some sentences are periodic — 'As virtue, of all objects, is allowed to be the most valuable, this species of philosophers paint her...' — suspending the main clause behind a conditional. Others are running, delivering their predication immediately and trailing qualifications: 'They make us feel the difference between vice and virtue; they excite and regulate our sentiments.' Both patterns coexist.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has performable rhythms — the tricolon 'entertainment, instruction, and reformation,' the parallel 'they excite and regulate... they make us feel' — and carries a measured, lecturing cadence suited to oral delivery. It is not flat bureaucratic prose, but neither does it have the dramatic personal urgency of oratory; it maintains a composed, philosophical evenness.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate and formal throughout: 'peculiar merit,' 'reformation of mankind,' 'illustrious examples,' 'probity,' 'academical,' 'sceptical.' The diction is elevated and philosophical, with no Anglo-Saxon plainness except in occasional monosyllables like 'paths' and 'steps.'
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its philosophical argument, but rhetorical figures surface visibly: the personification of virtue as 'her,' the tricolon enumerations, the parallel anaphora of 'They select... they place... they direct... they make us feel.' These figures are deliberate structural displays that draw some attention to the prose surface without overwhelming the content.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real weight — 'escapes,' 'creeps,' 'transport,' 'conceived' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns are also prominent: 'thought,' 'imagination,' 'power,' 'authority,' 'confusion,' 'contradiction.' Neither mode dominates; the prose moves between conceptual nouns and lively verbs.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Hypotactic subordination appears in relative clauses ('which not only escapes,' 'where nature is supposed') and conditionals, but the passage also coordinates through semicolons and 'and,' giving it a paratactic rhythm at the sentence level. The two modes alternate rather than one dominating.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence delays its main point behind 'at first view' and a long relative clause before arriving at the predication. The body/thought contrast sentence front-loads the body clause with its qualifications before releasing the thought clause as resolution. Suspension and delayed payoff are characteristic throughout.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has natural rhetorical emphases and dynamic range — the contrast between the body that 'creeps with pain and difficulty' and the thought that 'in an instant' transports us is performable and pointed. The final aphoristic sentence ('nor is any thing beyond the power of thought, except what implies an absolute contradiction') lands with deliberate finality.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Latinate diction throughout: 'incongruous,' 'conceive,' 'confined,' 'contradiction,' 'absolute,' 'restrained.' The register is formal philosophical prose, elevated but not ceremonial.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in service of its argument, but the body/thought antithesis and the closing aphorism display deliberate rhetorical shaping — the contrast is structured for effect, and the final sentence has the feel of a displayed figure. The surface is not invisible, but neither does it call sustained attention to itself.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Nominalizations appear throughout — 'observation,' 'examination,' 'invention,' 'connexion,' 'operation' — but they are counterbalanced by active verbs with human or mental agents: 'the mind must invent,' 'we discover,' 'I see,' 'may I not conceive.' The prose alternates between abstract noun-chains and direct verbal action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are heavily embedded through 'which,' 'that,' 'where,' 'when,' 'as,' and conditional constructions, creating layered subordination. Even the rhetorical questions contain nested relative clauses and conditional qualifications.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage mixes both modes: some sentences front-load conditions and qualifications before delivering the main predication ('Were any object presented to us... after what manner must the mind proceed?'), while others run forward immediately ('The mind can never possibly find the effect in the supposed cause'). The rhetorical questions at the close tend toward running structure.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person address ('I beseech you,' 'When I see, for instance'), the direct rhetorical questions ('May I not conceive?', 'Why then should we give the preference?'), and the emphatic italicized 'a priori' all create natural performance opportunities with clear rises, stresses, and pauses. The prose is designed for a reader who can hear Hume's argumentative voice.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate and formal diction: 'pronounce,' 'ascribes,' 'scrutiny,' 'arbitrary,' 'conceivable,' 'connexion,' 'impulse.' The register is philosophical and elevated throughout, though occasional plain Anglo-Saxon words ('stone,' 'ball,' 'falls') anchor the abstract argument in concrete examples.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative function — the language serves the philosophical demonstration — but deliberate rhetorical figures surface visibly: the anaphoric 'May not... May not... May not,' the italicized Latin phrase, and the repeated Billiard-ball example as a structural device all draw attention to the prose as a crafted performance of reasoning.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Nominalizations are present throughout — 'subsistence,' 'deductions,' 'operations,' 'succession' — but active verbs with agents also carry significant weight: 'she has implanted,' 'carries forward,' 'has taught,' 'secure.' Neither mode fully dominates; the prose moves between abstract noun-clusters and purposive verbal action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are deeply embedded through 'which,' 'that,' 'by which,' 'without,' 'though,' and 'as/so' constructions, creating multiple ranked levels of subordination. The final sentence alone contains at least four nested relative and adverbial clauses.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence delays its main predication ('it is not probable') behind a long fronted subordinate clause establishing the operation of the mind; the final sentence suspends its main clause ('so has she implanted') behind the full 'As nature has taught us' construction. Qualifications and conditions consistently precede resolution.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries a discernible philosophical persona — the 'I shall add' opening and the personification of nature as 'she' give it warmth and rhetorical presence — but the density of subordination and the abstract diction flatten the dynamic range available to a performer.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate and formal throughout: 'conformable,' 'subsistence,' 'fallacious,' 'correspondent,' 'actuated,' 'laboured deductions of the understanding.' The register is that of eighteenth-century philosophical discourse.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in that it serves its argument without ostentatious display, but the 'As nature has taught… so has she implanted' parallelism and the triadic 'which may… may discover… may be independent' construction draw deliberate attention to rhetorical structure, giving the surface a mild formal self-consciousness.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nominalizations dominate throughout — 'resistance,' 'exertion,' 'endeavour,' 'consciousness,' 'connexion,' 'impression,' 'sentiment' — chained with prepositional phrases ('idea of power,' 'command of the will,' 'impression from which this idea is copied'). Verbs are largely copular or weak ('is,' 'follows,' 'meets with,' 'is copied'), serving mainly to link nominal constructions.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'that,' 'which,' 'where,' 'without,' and participial constructions across multiple levels of subordination, particularly in the long periodic sentence beginning 'But, first, we attribute power.' The numbered objections (first, secondly) impose a logical hierarchy that is itself a hypotactic structure of argument.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage mixes both modes: the opening conclusion ('We may therefore conclude... that our idea of power is not copied') is periodic, suspending the main claim behind qualifications; but the numbered refutations run forward with main assertions followed by elaborating qualifications ('we attribute power to a vast number of objects, where we never can suppose...').
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person plural ('we may conclude,' 'we attribute,' 'we experience') and the adversarial structure of objection and rebuttal create a performable argumentative rhythm, and the italicized Latin terms (_nisus_, _à priori_) mark moments of deliberate stress; but the density of abstract nominalization flattens the dynamic range and resists full vocal performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'temerity,' 'inconceivable,' 'obliging,' 'exertion,' 'inanimate,' 'accurate,' 'connexion,' plus untranslated Latin (_nisus_, _à priori_). The register is consistently elevated philosophical prose with no Anglo-Saxon plainness.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in that it serves its philosophical argument without sustained sound-patterning or rhetorical display; but the italicized Latin terms, the numbered structural markers, and the self-conscious hedging ('I hope, without any temerity, though with assurance') draw momentary attention to the surface as a rhetorical performance of careful reasoning.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The prose is dominated by nominal constructions — 'Corrections and Improvements,' 'the Advantage of his last Corrections,' 'a Copy delivered by him' — with verbs largely reduced to 'has been,' 'were published,' 'is included,' 'is free.' Action is consistently suppressed into passive or stative constructions.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The modern prefatory sentences are largely paratactic, strung together as discrete declarative statements. The 1764 Editor's Note, however, is hypotactic, embedding qualifications through 'which,' 'from,' and participial phrases ('delivered by him,' 'communicated to the Editor') in a single long periodic structure.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The modern digitizer's sentences are running — short declaratives with immediate predication. The 1764 editorial sentence is periodic, suspending its main claim ('has not only been collated') behind accumulating qualifications about editions, corrections, and provenance.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is almost entirely bibliographic and administrative in character, offering no natural emphases, dynamic range, or performable personality. Both the modern prefatory note and the 1764 editor's note resist vocal delivery — they are reference text, not address.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The modern prefatory sentences use plain, functional diction ('published,' 'included,' 'recovered'), while the 1764 note rises toward formal Latinate register ('collated,' 'communicated,' 'lodged'). The overall effect is a middle register with occasional formal elevation.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is entirely instrumental — its purpose is to convey bibliographic and provenance information, and it draws no attention to its own surface through sound, figure, or structural display. The language is a pure vehicle for factual content.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real argumentative weight — 'puts an end to,' 'agreeing together,' 'make one body politic,' 'belongs to men' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns are also present: 'state of nature,' 'compact,' 'promises and bargains,' 'keeping of faith.' Neither mode dominates; the prose moves between conceptual nouns and active predication.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Subordinate clauses embed through 'since,' 'whether,' 'for,' 'though,' and 'as' constructions, creating layered qualification. The long central sentence — 'for it is not every compact... but only this one of agreeing... and make one body politic; other promises... and yet still be' — stacks conditions and exceptions inside each other.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Some sentences are periodic — 'since all princes and rulers... are in a state of nature, it is plain the world never was...' — holding the conclusion behind a subordinate clause; others run forward immediately, as in the final sentence where the main assertion arrives early and qualifications trail after.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person 'I have named' and the direct adversarial framing ('it is often asked as a mighty objection') give the prose a debating personality with natural emphatic stress points; but the long middle sentences, stacking legal distinctions, flatten into a more even, expository cadence that resists full performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is neither ceremonially Latinate nor plainly Anglo-Saxon — 'compact,' 'community,' 'politic,' 'reference' sit alongside 'truck,' 'men in the woods,' 'desert island.' The register is the educated plain style of seventeenth-century philosophical argument.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws no attention to its own surface — no sound patterns, no rhetorical figures, no self-conscious structural display. The concrete examples (the Swiss and the Indian, Garcilasso de la Vega) serve the argument instrumentally rather than as ornament, and the language disappears into its conceptual content.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs with human agents appear throughout — 'God gave,' 'he desired,' 'he had,' 'ought not to meddle' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns also carry significant weight: 'benefit,' 'conveniencies,' 'improvement,' 'covetousness,' 'industry.' Neither mode dominates; the prose moves between concrete action and abstract principle.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed deeply inside each other through 'since,' 'which,' 'that,' 'whereof,' and conditional 'if' constructions, creating multiple levels of subordination. The final long sentence is a cascade of embedded relative and conditional clauses that never fully resolves into a clean coordinate chain.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates between running sentences that deliver their main predication early ('God gave the world to men in common; but since...') and periodic constructions that front-load conditions before the main clause ('He that had as good left for his improvement, as was already taken up, needed not complain'). The final sentence is strongly periodic, suspending its main verb behind a long chain of qualifications.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries a discernible argumentative personality — the parenthetical aside '(and labour was to be his title to it;)' and the blunt 'it is plain he desired' invite vocal emphasis and a tone of reasoned rebuke. However, the dense subordination in the final sentence resists easy oral performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction mixes plain Anglo-Saxon words ('gave,' 'left,' 'ground,' 'pains,' 'reach') with Latinate abstractions ('conveniencies,' 'covetousness,' 'contentious,' 'industry'), producing an unmarked middle register characteristic of seventeenth-century philosophical prose aimed at a literate but non-specialist audience.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative purpose, but the parenthetical aside, the antithetical pairing of 'industrious and rational' against 'quarrelsome and contentious,' and the deliberate repetition of 'as good left' draw mild attention to the rhetorical surface without fully foregrounding it as display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real argumentative weight — 'loosen,' 'drop off,' 'leave,' 'provide,' 'govern,' 'preserve, nourish, and educate' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns are also present: 'subjection,' 'preservation,' 'improvement,' 'obligation,' 'workmanship.' Neither mode dominates; the prose moves between concrete verbal action and abstract nominal framing.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are embedded through 'though,' 'till,' 'which,' 'who,' 'not as... but,' and participial constructions, creating layered subordination. The long sentence in Sect. 56 — 'but to supply the defects... till the improvement... hath removed them, Adam and Eve... were, by the law of nature, under an obligation' — is a characteristic hypotactic suspension.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The swaddling-clothes sentence is running, delivering its main image early and trailing qualifications; but the Sect. 56 sentence is periodic, front-loading a long conditional purpose clause ('but to supply the defects of this imperfect state, till the improvement of growth and age hath removed them') before the main predication arrives. Both patterns appear.
claude_justifications.voice: The swaddling-clothes metaphor and the tricolon 'preserve, nourish, and educate' offer natural performance points with emphasis and rhythm, and 'I confess' gives a personal, speakerly opening; but much of the prose — especially the long Sect. 56 sentence — is too syntactically dense for easy oral delivery.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction blends Latinate abstractions ('jurisdiction,' 'subjection,' 'preservation,' 'obligation') with plain Anglo-Saxon vocabulary ('born,' 'weak,' 'grow up,' 'drop off,' 'own maker'). The register is neither ceremonially high nor colloquially low — a characteristic Lockean plain-philosophical middle.
claude_justifications.opacity: The swaddling-clothes extended metaphor draws deliberate attention to the prose surface as a rhetorical figure, and the tricolon 'preserve, nourish, and educate' is a visible structural display; but most of the passage is instrumentally transparent, serving the argument without foregrounding its own language.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage mixes nominal constructions ('ignorance of causes,' 'Encrease of Science,' 'Benefit of man-kind') with active verbal energy ('set men out of their way,' 'snuffed and purged,' 'wandering amongst absurdities'). The famous aphoristic sequence — 'Reason is the Pace; Encrease of Science, the Way' — is heavily nominal, but the surrounding argument moves through active verbs.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between hypotactic subordination in the argumentative sections ('they that have no Science... than men, that by mis-reasoning... fall upon') and the strikingly paratactic aphoristic sequence at the center, where parallel noun-copula constructions are coordinated by semicolons rather than embedded.

The argumentative sentences front-load conditions and causes before delivering conclusions, and 'To conclude' signals a gathered, delayed resolution.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is highly performable — the aphoristic sequence ('Reason is the Pace; Encrease of Science, the Way') invites emphatic oral delivery with natural stress and pause, and the rhetorical turn 'And on the contrary' sets up a voiced antithesis. The Ignes Fatui metaphor and the closing tricolon ('contention, and sedition, or contempt') have the cadence of pulpit oratory.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Latinate and formal throughout — 'Perspicuous,' 'ambiguity,' 'Prudence,' 'absurdities,' 'contention,' 'sedition' — with the elevated register of seventeenth-century philosophical prose. The capitalization of abstract nouns further marks the ceremonial, high-register treatment.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws sustained attention to its own surface through the extended metaphor of light and path ('Light,' 'Pace,' 'Way,' 'End'), the deliberate structural parallelism of the aphoristic sequence, and the vivid figure of Ignes Fatui (will-o'-the-wisps). These rhetorical devices foreground the language itself as a formal, self-conscious display rather than a transparent vehicle for argument.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Nominalizations are present (Fortification, Defence, Victory, Value, Worth, Price, judgement) but active verbs carry real argumentative weight — 'conferre,' 'determines,' 'esteemed,' 'rate themselves.' The prose moves between noun-anchored definitions and verb-driven assertions without either fully dominating.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Hypotactic embedding appears in the parenthetical aside and the 'because/namely/yet/because' chains of the opening sentence, but the latter half of the passage shifts to paratactic parallel constructions — 'is of great Price in time of War... but in Peace not so' — coordinating examples in balanced series.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence is periodic, suspending its main point through a chain of 'because' and 'yet/because' clauses before resolving; but the definitional sentences ('The Value, or WORTH of a man, is...') and the parallel soldier/judge examples are running, delivering their predications immediately and trailing qualifications.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is highly performable — the parenthetical '(the Midwife passing with the vulgar for the Mother)' invites a conspiratorial aside, the parallel soldier/judge sentences have a crisp antithetical rhythm, and the closing 'yet their true Value is no more than it is esteemed by others' lands with deliberate finality. Emphasis and dynamic range are built into the structure.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Latinate abstractions (Fortification, Instruments, conductor, imminent, uncorrupt) coexist with plain Anglo-Saxon directness ('the seller, but the buyer determines the Price,' 'rate themselves at the highest Value they can'). The register is characteristically Hobbesian — formal argument delivered in blunt, demystifying terms.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws attention to its own surface through the extended midwife/mother conceit, the deliberate capitalization of key terms (Value, WORTH, Price, Power) as rhetorical markers, the antithetical parallel structure of the soldier/judge examples, and the aphoristic snap of the closing sentence — all of which foreground the writing as a crafted rhetorical performance.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nominalizations are prominent — Sincerity, Reputation, Injustice, Cruelty, Dominion, Dignity — but they are balanced against active verbal constructions: 'taketh away,' 'make men to fall,' 'believeth there is,' 'reap benefit by.' The prose moves between noun-anchored definitions and verb-driven demonstrations.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are deeply embedded through 'that,' 'which,' 'as,' 'because,' and 'when' constructions, creating multiple levels of subordination — 'that which taketh away... is the doing or saying of such things, as appeare to be signes, that what they require... is not believed.' Coordinate 'and/or' chains appear but serve subordinate rather than structural roles.
