claude_justifications.voice: The passage has moments of genuine performability — the rhetorical turn 'But his formulation... were badly hampered,' the crisp parallel 'growing is growth, developing is development,' and the ironic quotation of Froebel's circle rationale all invite vocal emphasis. However, the surrounding abstract nominalization and passive constructions flatten much of the prose into an even, lecturing tone.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate and philosophical diction throughout: 'immanent,' 'actuating,' 'manifestation,' 'realization,' 'criterion,' 'implicit,' 'explicit.' The register is that of academic philosophical exposition, with only occasional plain Anglo-Saxon moments ('wrapped up,' 'sleeping within him').
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative intent — it aims to convey a philosophical critique and the language mostly serves that purpose without calling attention to itself. However, the deliberate parallel construction 'growing is growth, developing is development' and the ironic deployment of Froebel's own quoted language ('because it is a symbol of the collective life of mankind in general') represent moments of self-conscious rhetorical display that briefly foreground the surface.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nominalizations are present throughout — stimulation, response, separation, endosmosis, interchange — but active verbs also carry significant weight: 'educate,' 'loses,' 'prevents,' 'tends to be,' 'becomes.' Neither mode fully dominates, though the final catalogue of noun-predicate constructions ('their art becomes,' 'their wealth luxurious') tips slightly toward nominal compression.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between hypotactic embedding ('in order to have,' 'when the free interchange... is arrested,' 'which educate some into masters') and paratactic accumulation, most visibly in the final asyndetic series of parallel 'their X' clauses. Neither mode is sustained long enough to dominate.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Several sentences are periodic — 'In order to have a large number of values in common, all the members of the group must have...' and 'Otherwise, the influences which educate some into masters, educate others into slaves' — but others run forward immediately, and the final sentence delivers its subject early and trails a long coordinate series of predications.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has performable moments — the parallel 'educate some into masters, educate others into slaves' invites rhetorical stress, and the final catalogue builds to a climax — but the impersonal, third-person analytical mode and abstract diction flatten much of the dynamic range a speaker could exploit.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate and formal throughout: 'endosmosis,' 'equable,' 'fastidious,' 'perceptible,' 'privileged and subject-class,' 'modes of life-experience.' The diction is that of philosophical and social-scientific discourse, with no Anglo-Saxon plainness except in isolated words.
claude_justifications.opacity: The passage is largely transparent in its argumentative function, but the final sentence's anaphoric 'their X' series — 'their culture,' 'their art,' 'their wealth,' 'their knowledge,' 'their manners' — draws attention to its own rhetorical structure as a deliberate display of parallel accumulation, briefly foregrounding the surface.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Heavy nominalization throughout: 'the futility of trying to establish the aim,' 'prospective points of view,' 'the statement of aim,' 'the basis of the defects and needs,' 'domination by authority.' Abstract nouns chained with prepositional phrases carry most of the conceptual weight, though occasional active verbs ('we take,' 'we frame,' 'we tend') provide some relief.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'since,' 'which,' 'that,' and 'whatever,' creating layered subordination — 'since general aims are but prospective points of view from which to survey... and estimate.' The passage builds hierarchical logical structure rather than coordinate chains.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates between running sentences that deliver their predication early ('We have just pointed out the futility...') and periodic constructions that front-load conditions before the main clause ('It is, then, no paradox requiring explanation that...'). Neither pattern dominates consistently.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person plural 'we' creates a mild rhetorical presence and some sentences carry performable emphasis ('We tend rather to frame,' 'we take for granted'), but the abstract nominalized diction flattens much of the dynamic range and resists full vocal performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction blends Latinate abstractions ('subordinates,' 'prospective,' 'contemporary,' 'disorganized') with plainer constructions ('taking care of themselves fairly well,' 'things which do not require emphasis'), landing in an educated but not ceremonial middle register characteristic of philosophical exposition.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative intent, but occasional rhetorical gestures — the italicized 'no paradox' (rendered here as 'DO paradox'), the chiastic final sentence balancing 'domination by authority' against 'disorganized individual activities' — draw brief attention to the surface as deliberate structural display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry much of the narrative weight — 'ran wild,' 'increased,' 'exported,' 'multiplied,' 'fell upon,' 'left him dead' — but the passage also relies on nominal constructions like 'the rapid spread of,' 'an indication of the vast numbers,' and 'the result being.' The argumentative framing is noun-heavy while the illustrative examples are verb-driven.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage combines both modes: hypotactic subordination appears in the long opening sentence ('As the facts now stated... some direct evidence must be adduced') and in relative clauses throughout, while the narrative examples often proceed paratactically through coordinate 'and' chains ('Cattle were afterwards taken... and in 1587... and 35,444 from St. Domingo').
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence and several topic sentences are periodic, front-loading conditions and qualifications before the main predication ('That even the larger animals... is shown by'). But the illustrative passages — especially the Columbus anecdote and the asses of Quito — run forward in narrative sequence, delivering information as it accumulates.
claude_justifications.voice: The vivid anecdotes — asses biting a horse to death, herds of 8,000 cattle — offer natural performance moments with genuine dramatic range, but the argumentative scaffolding ('some direct evidence of actual cases must be adduced,' 'an indication of the vast numbers') is flat and resistant to vocal emphasis.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The prose occupies a Victorian scientific middle register — neither the high formality of parliamentary oratory nor the plain Anglo-Saxon of Hemingway. Latinate terms ('favourable conditions,' 'perpetual destruction,' 'indication') coexist with plain concrete nouns (cattle, hogs, hides, pigs, mouths).
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is entirely instrumental — it exists to convey evidence and argument, not to display its own surface. There are no sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or self-conscious structural gestures; the language effaces itself in service of the accumulating empirical case.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is dense with nominalizations and noun phrases: 'immense antiquity,' 'apparent absence,' 'useful productions,' 'cultivation nor selection,' 'ancient civilisation.' Verbs are largely stative or passive ('has been inhabited,' 'has been carried on,' 'has given rise') rather than active and agentive.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are embedded through 'notwithstanding that,' 'as indicated by,' 'though,' and participial constructions ('these countries having been'). Multiple levels of subordination stack qualification upon qualification before resolution.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence is running — the main predication ('explains the apparent absence') arrives early — but subsequent sentences front-load participial and conditional material ('These countries having been...,' 'In North America, however, where...') before delivering their main clauses, creating a periodic tendency.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has some performable rhythm — the contrastive 'however' and the emphatic 'no fewer than thirty-three' invite mild stress — but the passive constructions and impersonal framing ('neither cultivation nor selection has been carried on') flatten the dynamic range considerably.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'antiquity,' 'sufficiently,' 'comparatively,' 'uncivilised,' 'prehistoric,' 'civilisation.' The register is that of Victorian scientific prose — elevated and impersonal.
claude_justifications.opacity: The language is entirely instrumental, directing attention to the argument about plant cultivation and civilisation rather than to its own surface. There are no sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or self-conscious structural display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Heavy nominalization throughout — 'difficulty,' 'differentiation,' 'perpetuation,' 'elimination,' 'correlation' — chained with prepositional phrases ('as to how,' 'by the bar of,' 'by heredity,' 'by disuse'). Active verbs appear but are frequently passive or copular ('are evaded,' 'is intelligible,' 'are preserved'), suppressing agency.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed deeply through 'that,' 'which,' 'unless,' 'until,' and 'if' constructions, creating multiple levels of subordination. The quoted passage within the passage adds a further layer of embedded hypotaxis.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence is periodic, suspending its main verb ('is evaded') behind a long nominal subject and conditional qualifier. But the rhetorical question and the final sentence run forward, delivering their main predications early and trailing qualifications afterward.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has argumentative personality — the direct challenge 'But this is entirely begging the question' and the rhetorical question create performable moments of emphasis and force. However, the surrounding technical and nominalized passages flatten the dynamic range.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'perpetuated,' 'physiological,' 'differentiated,' 'intelligible,' 'correlated,' 'accumulated.' The register is that of Victorian scientific controversy — elevated and technical.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative function, but the italicized phrases within the quotation ('should at first be allowed to arise,' 'be allowed to perpetuate themselves') draw deliberate attention to the language being contested, creating a meta-linguistic moment of surface display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry the narrative of scientific observation — 'proved,' 'found,' 'showed,' 'wanders,' 'rests,' 'spinning' — but nominalizations and noun-heavy constructions also appear: 'the action of the coloured light,' 'the means of clearing up,' 'the application of various surrounding colours.' Neither mode dominates consistently.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are embedded through 'that,' 'when,' 'which,' 'whose,' and 'and that' constructions, creating layered subordination — particularly in the long sentence beginning 'He showed that the action...' and the sentence describing Mrs. Barber's findings with three embedded participial conditions.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Many sentences are running, delivering their main predication early and trailing qualifications ('He showed that...,' 'Mrs. Barber found that...'), but several sentences front-load conditional or temporal material before the main clause ('When this is found it rests quietly,' 'After a caterpillar has done feeding it wanders'), creating a periodic tendency in the more explanatory passages.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has a measured, lecturing quality that rewards careful reading aloud — the enumerated conditions of Mrs. Barber's observations and the final summarizing sentence have natural rhetorical emphasis — but the scientific reportorial mode keeps it from strong vocal performance, with no first-person presence and a generally even, informational tone.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is educated but not heavily Latinate — plain words like 'wanders,' 'rests,' 'spinning,' 'fences,' 'walls' mix with more formal terms like 'quiescence,' 'assimilated,' 'transformation,' and 'phenomena,' producing a middle register characteristic of Victorian popular science writing.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is entirely instrumental — it conveys experimental findings and causal sequences without drawing attention to its own surface through sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or structural display. The language is a window onto the scientific content, not an object of attention in itself.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real weight — 'refused,' 'rejected,' 'eaten,' 'serve to distinguish' — but nominal constructions also appear: 'warning colours,' 'protective colouration,' 'insect-eating animals.' Neither mode dominates; the prose moves between taxonomic naming and observed action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Some sentences are paratactic chains joined by 'and,' while others embed subordinate clauses through 'which,' 'though,' and relative constructions. The passage alternates between coordinate listing and embedded qualification without settling into either pattern.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Main predications arrive early in nearly every sentence — 'We all know,' 'Most of the great tribe are distasteful,' 'Our red and black Telephoridae were found' — with qualifications and elaborations trailing afterward.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has a lecturing, authoritative personality — 'We all know,' 'no one of which' — and the accumulation of named authorities (Jenner Weir, Mr. Belt) gives it a confident, performable cadence, though the taxonomic passages flatten into enumeration.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Latinate scientific terminology (Malacoderms, Coccinellidae, Lampyridae, Telephoridae) sits alongside plain Anglo-Saxon diction ('small birds,' 'lady-birds,' 'glow-worms,' 'greedily eaten'), producing a characteristic Victorian natural-history blend of technical and vernacular.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative function, but the parenthetical common names ('soldiers and sailors,' 'fireflies and glow-worms,' 'lady-birds') and the rhythmic accumulation of examples draw mild attention to the surface as a rhetorical display of taxonomic authority.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry the narrative forward — lived, accompanied, rewarded, dug, built, called, held, handed, visited — but the prose also accumulates nouns in inventory-style lists (health, rank, income, domain, house, wife, daughters) and nominal phrases (prodigious antiquity, successive barons, present lord). Neither mode dominates; the passage alternates between action and enumeration.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The historical genealogy sections run paratactically through coordinated 'and' chains ('dug a mote and built a chateau, and called it'), while other sentences embed subordinate clauses ('when a younger son accompanied,' 'before he dies,' 'after this short absence'). The two modes coexist without either fully dominating.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and trail qualifications and elaborations afterward — 'His family was of prodigious antiquity; seven successive barons had already flourished...' The one periodic gesture ('Thus rooted in his native Brittany, Henri Lionel...') is the exception rather than the rule.
claude_justifications.voice: The parenthetical aside ('the worthy Saxons turned this into Borreper without delay') and the ironic qualification ('as fortunate as any man can be pronounced before he dies') introduce a dry, performable wit that lifts the prose above bureaucratic flatness, though the genealogical inventory sections resist vocal emphasis.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is predominantly formal and Latinate — antiquity, prodigious, lineage, veneration, domain, celebrated — with French proper nouns reinforcing an aristocratic, elevated register throughout.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its narrative function, but the parenthetical on the Saxon corruption of 'Beaurepaire,' the ironic mortality clause, and the full ceremonial deployment of the hero's five-part name ('Henri Lionel Marie St. Quentin de Beaurepaire') draw momentary attention to the surface as deliberate rhetorical gestures.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs drive the narrative throughout — parted, trusted, told, roused, expanded, spread, walked, whirled — with human agents performing physical and emotional actions. Nominalizations appear (revelation, understanding, protestation) but are outnumbered by the kinetic verb chain.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between paratactic coordinate chains ('The sun set, and the night came, and the stars glittered') and hypotactic embedding ('who had cast many a furtive glance,' 'let who will betray thee'). Neither mode dominates; the two rhythms alternate for tonal variety.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most narrative sentences are running — main predications arrive early and trail qualifications — but the apostrophe to Youth ('let who will betray thee; let who will sneer at thee') builds periodically through anaphoric accumulation before releasing into the main assertion, and the final sentence suspends its resolution through a long series of appositives.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is emphatically performable: the direct apostrophe ('Ah! generous Youth'), the anaphoric 'let who will' triplet, the exclamatory rhythms, and the final cadence ('a heart on fire; and youth the fuel, and the flame vestal') all demand vocal emphasis, dynamic range, and rhetorical pause. A distinct narrator's personality is audible throughout.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The passage moves fluidly between low Anglo-Saxon diction for physical action ('went home on wings,' 'walked up and down for hours') and elevated Latinate or literary diction for emotional commentary ('pinions,' 'vestal,' 'guardian angel,' 'exalted'). The mixing is deliberate and tonal, shifting register to signal ironic distance or lyric elevation.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws sustained attention to its own surface through anaphora ('let who will… let who will… let me'), the classical allusion embedded in 'vestal,' the rhetorical apostrophe to Youth, the semicolon-fragmented final sentence that mimics breathless accumulation, and the conspicuous inversion 'the flame vestal.' These are deliberate structural and figural displays, not transparent vehicles for content.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is driven by rapid physical action verbs — looked, turned, welling, recovering, cried, flew, reversing, spun — with almost no nominalizations. Even abstract states are rendered through bodily action rather than noun phrases.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Paratactic coordination dominates the narration ('looked, and turned,' 'flew to the wheelbarrow, and, reversing it, spun'), but hypotactic subordination appears in the dialogue and qualifying clauses ('recovering himself by an effort of the will,' 'in his present condition').
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Main predications arrive immediately and qualifications trail behind — 'Edouard looked, and turned sick, for there was a gash' — with no suspended main clauses. The prose rushes forward in the manner of urgent action narrative.
claude_justifications.voice: The dialogue is highly performable with natural emphases, exclamations, and tonal shifts — from the reassuring 'Courage, my lad!' to the dismissive 'To the devil with Jacintha and her wood too!' The prose has clear dynamic range between the narrator's urgency and the characters' distinct registers.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The narration uses middle-register diction while the dialogue shifts between elevated exclamation ('Thank Heaven,' 'To the devil') and plain colloquial speech ('Ye must not do that'), creating a register contrast between characters.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its narrative function, but the parenthetical reversal 'and, reversing it, spun a lot of billet out' and the rhythmic urgency of the dialogue sequences draw mild attention to the surface as a performance of haste and crisis.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is driven by imperative and active verbs — 'go,' 'send,' 'ask,' 'revenged,' 'crushed,' 'turned' — with the baroness's speech especially action-oriented and physically urgent. Nominalizations are sparse; even abstract states are rendered through bodily action ('lie down and die,' 'ask this favor on my knees').
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The baroness's direct speech is largely paratactic — short declarative and exclamatory units strung together with minimal subordination — while the narrator's framing sentences ('The poor baroness, all whose pride the iron law, with its iron gripe, had crushed into dismay and terror, appealed to him') are densely hypotactic with embedded relative clauses.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication immediately and trail qualifications afterward — 'I did not know I was doing anything wrong,' 'I will go, gentlemen, I will go.' The one periodic exception is the narrator's long sentence suspending 'appealed to him' behind a heavy participial phrase.
claude_justifications.voice: The passage is almost entirely direct speech and is saturated with performable affect — exclamations, apostrophes, rhetorical questions, shifts from pleading to accusation to supplication. Natural emphases are everywhere: 'I will go, gentlemen, I WILL go'; 'not from the soil where my Henri is laid'; 'NEW BARON' in capitals.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The baroness's speech is predominantly plain and Anglo-Saxon in diction ('go,' 'house,' 'born,' 'knees,' 'die'), while the narrator's intrusions rise to a higher, more Latinate register ('domain,' 'dismay,' 'appealed,' 'comprehend'), creating a deliberate contrast between the woman's stripped grief and the law's formal machinery.
claude_justifications.opacity: The narrator's framing sentence — 'the iron law, with its iron gripe' — is self-consciously figured, with the repeated 'iron' drawing attention to its own rhetorical surface. Elsewhere the prose is largely transparent, the language serving the dramatic situation without calling attention to itself.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is driven by active verbs with a human agent throughout — 'I did start,' 'I have turned,' 'I say to myself,' 'I see,' 'it gives me a knock,' 'you speak.' Nominalizations are nearly absent; the prose moves through actions, observations, and direct speech acts.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are strung together with 'and' and semicolons in coordinate chains — 'I did start... But since I have been... and seen... I have turned... and I say.' Subordination exists but is shallow; the dominant movement is additive and sequential rather than hierarchically embedded.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Main predications arrive immediately and qualifications trail behind — 'I did start with a good motive at first, that there's no denying.' There is no suspension of the main clause; Raynal speaks as he thinks, forward and without delay.
claude_justifications.voice: This is direct dramatic speech with a fully realized personality behind it — blunt, self-deprecating, cajoling, abrupt. Natural emphases are everywhere: 'a knock here,' 'not so mighty disinterested,' 'Take a day. Take two if you like.' The prose practically performs itself.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is predominantly plain and colloquial Anglo-Saxon — 'look here,' 'a knock here,' 'the fellows,' 'good-day.' The French address 'mademoiselle' and the mild formality of 'disinterested' are the only departures from an otherwise vernacular soldier's register.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent — it serves character revelation and dramatic situation without calling attention to its surface. However, the rhetorical structure of Raynal's self-correction ('So you see I am not so mighty disinterested') and his parallel imperatives ('Take a day... Take two if you like') show a mild degree of deliberate rhetorical shaping that surfaces briefly before dissolving back into colloquial directness.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Heavy nominalization throughout: 'substance of a course of lectures,' 'novelty of such an attempt,' 'prejudices usually conceived against any innovations in the established mode of education,' 'a mixture of pride and gratitude.' The prose moves through prepositional phrase chains anchored to abstract nouns rather than through active verbs.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The long central sentence embeds clause within clause — 'notwithstanding the novelty... and the prejudices... he had the satisfaction to find (and he acknowledges it...) that his endeavours were encouraged... by those... whose good opinion...' — creating multiple ranked levels of subordination held in suspension.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The main predication ('he had the satisfaction to find... that his endeavours were encouraged') is delayed behind a long front-loaded participial and prepositional structure ('notwithstanding the novelty of such an attempt... and the prejudices usually conceived...'), requiring the reader to hold considerable subordinate material before the resolution arrives.
claude_justifications.voice: The third-person self-reference ('the author,' 'he') creates a formal ceremonial distance that partially suppresses vocal performance, yet the parenthetical aside '(and he acknowledges it with a mixture of pride and gratitude)' introduces a personal warmth that invites mild emphasis and dynamic variation.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Consistently formal Latinate diction throughout: 'patronized,' 'endeavours,' 'innovations,' 'prejudices,' 'principally desirous,' 'notwithstanding.' The register is that of eighteenth-century learned prose, ceremonial and elevated.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in that it serves its prefatory argument without conspicuous sound patterning, yet the elaborate suspended periodic structure and the self-conscious parenthetical aside draw mild attention to the prose surface as a formal rhetorical performance rather than plain communication.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Heavy nominalization throughout — tradition, experience, constitution, authority, convulsions, overthrow — chained with prepositional phrases ('of the empire,' 'of the conqueror,' 'of their canon law from this original'). Active verbs appear but are often passive or weak copulas ('was introduced,' 'were performed,' 'were conferred'), and the nominal weight dominates the prose's center of gravity.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed deeply through 'who,' 'which,' 'where,' 'being,' and participial constructions, creating multiple ranked levels of subordination within single sentences. The long final sentence is a showcase of hypotactic layering — nations adopting law, blending customs, qualified by parenthetical and participial phrases stacked inside each other.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage mixes both tendencies: some sentences open with front-loaded subordinate material ('A copy of Justinian's pandects, being newly discovered at Amalfi, soon brought...') that is mildly periodic, while others trail qualifications after an early main predication in running fashion. The final long sentence is strongly periodic, suspending its main verb 'adopted' behind a long participial buildup.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries a discernible authorial personality — the dry irony of 'not so heartily relished' and 'shoals' gives it some performable edge — but the long embedded clauses and passive constructions flatten the dynamic range, making sustained oral performance difficult without losing the thread.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'pandects,' 'faculty,' 'feodal,' 'constitutions,' 'convulsions consequent upon,' 'extensive authority.' The register is consistently elevated legal-historical prose, with no concession to plain Anglo-Saxon vocabulary.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in that it serves its historical argument without conspicuous rhetorical display, but moments of deliberate stylistic choice surface — the sardonic 'in shoals,' the rhythmic tricolon 'exercises were performed, lectures read, and degrees conferred,' and the balanced antithesis of 'more extensive, in others a more confined authority' draw brief attention to the surface.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nominalizations are present throughout — 'foundations,' 'preservation,' 'convention,' 'compulsion,' 'conquest' — but active verbs with agents also carry significant weight: 'met together,' 'entered into,' 'extended its limits,' 'subdivided itself,' 'keeps mankind together.' Neither mode fully dominates; the prose moves between conceptual abstraction and narrative action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are consistently embedded through 'which,' 'that,' 'wherein,' 'though,' 'as,' and 'when,' creating layered subordination. The final long sentence is a showcase of hypotactic structure, with multiple 'that' clauses stacked inside a concessive 'though' construction.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates between the two modes: the opening sentence is running (main predication first, then qualification), while the final sentence is strongly periodic, suspending the main assertion ('yet it is the sense of their weakness') behind a long concessive clause. Mid-passage sentences tend toward running with trailing relative clauses.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person plural ('we can believe') and the italicized emphases on 'sense' and 'keeps' create moments of performable stress and rhetorical address, and the dismissive aside ('too wild to be seriously admitted') has a speakable ironic tone. However, the density of subordination and abstraction in much of the passage flattens the dynamic range available to a reader.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate and formal throughout: 'theoretical,' 'contradictory,' 'primitive origin,' 'preservation,' 'pastoral state,' 'convention,' 'actuated,' 'imperfection.' The diction is that of eighteenth-century learned prose, with no concession to plain Anglo-Saxon vocabulary.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative function, moving through a logical sequence without calling attention to sound or figure. However, the italicization of 'sense' and 'keeps' is a deliberate rhetorical display, and the final sentence's tricolon ('that demonstrates… that therefore is… as well as the cement') foregrounds its own structural symmetry enough to register as mild opacity.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Nominalizations and legal abstractions are present throughout (existence, derogation, conveyance, prerogative, allowance), but active constructions also appear with human or legal agents performing actions ('he has a right,' 'the other cannot claim,' 'the king purchases'). Neither mode fully dominates.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Subordinate clauses embed through 'if,' 'that,' 'which,' 'where,' and 'yet' constructions, creating conditional and relative hierarchies — especially in the gavelkind example, where multiple qualifying clauses rank and restrict the main proposition.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Some sentences are periodic, front-loading conditionals before the main predication ('if both are really customs, then both are of equal antiquity'), while others run forward immediately ('Customs, in derogation of the common law, must be construed strictly'). The two modes alternate throughout.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has a lecturing, expository personality — the italicized emphasis on 'consistent,' the direct logical refutations ('which to say of contradictory customs is absurd'), and the numbered structure give it a mild performative quality, though it lacks the rhetorical heat of oratory.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly Latinate legal diction throughout: 'derogation,' 'prerogative,' 'feoffment,' 'gavelkind,' 'demise,' 'prescribes,' 'impower.' The register is formal and technical, characteristic of eighteenth-century common-law exposition.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative function, but the numbered structure, italicized keywords, bracketed citations, and the self-conscious closing summary ('And thus much for the second part of the leges non scriptae') draw mild attention to the text's own organizational surface.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The prose is organized around nominal definitions and etymological derivations — 'division,' 'administration,' 'government,' 'corruption,' 'jurisdictions' — with verbs largely serving as copulas or passive constructions ('is derived,' 'is intrusted,' 'is now totally devolved'). The subject matter itself drives nominalization: this is a taxonomy of administrative units, and the prose enacts that taxonomy through noun-heavy structure.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between hypotactic relative clauses ('to whom the government of it was intrusted,' 'still called in Latin vice-comes') and paratactic enumeration ('the north, the east, and the west-riding'). Individual sentences tend toward hypotaxis, but the paragraph as a whole proceeds by coordinate accumulation of parallel facts.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and then trail qualifications, etymological glosses, and parenthetical elaborations afterward — 'This he usually exercised by his deputy, still called in Latin vice-comes, and in English the sheriff...' The information accumulates after the main clause rather than suspending it.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has a measured, lecturing quality that rewards careful oral delivery — the etymological asides and parenthetical glosses create natural pauses and mild emphasis — but the impersonal, definitional mode suppresses dramatic range and personal presence, keeping it short of strongly voiced.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction dominates: 'comitatus,' 'vice-comes,' 'intermediate jurisdictions,' 'civil administration,' 'subordination,' 'antiently.' The Latin etymologies are displayed rather than translated away, signaling a learned, legal-encyclopedic register throughout.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its expository function — it aims to convey information about administrative divisions — but the foregrounded etymological display (Saxon, Latin, and Norman derivations set in italics and explained) draws intermittent attention to language itself as an object of inquiry, creating moments of deliberate surface visibility.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage mixes active legal verbs — 'may claim,' 'may issue,' 'can send,' 'shall be banished,' 'shall recover' — with nominal constructions like 'personal liberty,' 'royal prerogative,' 'express direction,' and 'private action.' The legal enumeration of penalties drives toward verb-style, but the subject matter generates substantial nominalization.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'unless,' 'that,' 'who,' 'which,' and 'where' constructions, creating ranked hierarchical subordination — especially in the long final sentence enumerating the habeas corpus provisions, where multiple 'that' clauses nest inside each other.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates between running sentences that deliver their main predication early ('The king indeed may issue out his writ') and periodic constructions that front qualifications before the main clause, as in the long habeas corpus sentence where conditions and exceptions precede the legal consequences.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries genuine performable energy — the emphatic 'no power on earth,' the parenthetical aside '(that second magna carta, and stable bulwark of our liberties),' and the rhetorical 'no not even a criminal' all invite vocal stress and dynamic range, though the dense statutory enumeration at the close flattens the performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate legal diction throughout: 'prerogative,' 'commonwealth,' 'praemunire,' 'inhabit­ant,' 'aiders and abettors,' 'incapable.' The register is consistently elevated, drawing on both common-law technical vocabulary and classical legal Latin.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its instrumental legal purpose, but moments of deliberate rhetorical display — the italicized Latin phrases, the parenthetical encomium on habeas corpus, the emphatic tricolon 'disabled… shall incur… incapable' — draw attention to the surface as a piece of considered public writing, not merely a legal digest.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage contains significant nominalization ('jurisdiction,' 'denomination,' 'misgovernment,' 'omnipotence') and prepositional chains, but is also driven by strong active verbs in the anaphoric 'It can' series — 'regulate,' 'alter,' 'change,' 'create.' The two tendencies coexist rather than one dominating.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The 'It can... It can... It can...' series is strongly paratactic, coordinating parallel assertions in a rhetorical chain; but the surrounding sentences are hypotactic, embedding subordinate clauses through 'which,' 'that,' 'as,' and 'if,' creating multiple levels of qualification.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The 'It can' sentences are running — main predications arrive immediately and trail examples afterward. But the final long sentence is periodic, suspending its conclusion ('the subjects of this kingdom are left without all manner of remedy') behind a chain of conditional and participial qualifications.
claude_justifications.voice: The anaphoric 'It can... It can... It can...' series is built for oral delivery and rhetorical crescendo, with natural stress points and dynamic range. The embedded Latin quotation, the named authorities (Coke, Burleigh, Hale), and the closing apothegm all invite vocal performance and emphasis.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout — 'transcendent,' 'jurisdiction,' 'ecclesiastical,' 'denominations,' 'abrogating,' 'despotic,' 'probity,' 'apothegm' — with embedded Latin and ceremonial legal register consistent with eighteenth-century parliamentary discourse.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws deliberate attention to its own surface through the anaphoric 'It can' series, the embedded Latin quotation with its triple superlative structure, the catalogue of gerunds ('making, confirming, enlarging, restraining, abrogating, repealing, reviving'), and the rhetorical figure of 'omnipotence of parliament' — all of which foreground structural and rhetorical display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs drive the procedural logic throughout — passes, rejected, agreed, send, remains, settle, adjust, dropped, deposited — with human and institutional agents performing discrete actions. Nominalizations are present (concurrence, amendments, altercations) but subordinate to the verb-driven procedural chain.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between conditional hypotaxis ('if rejected... but if it is agreed... if the commons disagree') and paratactic coordination ('and the bill remains... and when both houses have done'). The conditional 'if/but if' structure creates a branching decision-tree logic that is neither purely embedded nor purely coordinate.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and append qualifications afterward — 'the lords send a message by two masters in chancery (or sometimes two of the judges) that they have agreed.' The conditional 'if' clauses that open some sentences create mild periodicity, but the main clause typically arrives quickly.
claude_justifications.voice: The procedural enumeration and parallel 'if/but if' structure creates a readable, almost pedagogical rhythm that could be performed as a clear oral recitation, though without dramatic range or personal emphasis. The Latin insertions and parenthetical qualifications flatten the vocal texture somewhat.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal legal-parliamentary diction throughout: 'sub silentio,' 'mutatis mutandis,' 'engrossing,' 'masters in chancery,' 'royal assent,' 'concurrence.' The register is consistently elevated and technical, characteristic of eighteenth-century legal exposition.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is entirely instrumental — it exists to convey procedural information and draws no attention to its own surface. The parallel conditional structure is functional rather than ornamental, and there are no sound patterns, rhetorical figures, or self-conscious stylistic display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Nominalizations are present throughout — equality, conditions, influence, direction, tenor, maxims, habits — but they are animated by active verbs with a first-person agent: 'struck me,' 'I discovered,' 'I perceived,' 'it creates,' 'engenders,' 'suggests,' 'modifies.' The nouns carry the conceptual weight while the verbs carry the rhetorical momentum.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'which,' 'that,' 'by giving,' 'by imparting,' and 'and that' constructions, creating layered subordination. The final sentence in particular nests a relative clause inside a comparative structure inside a main clause.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates strategies: 'Amongst the novel objects... nothing struck me' is periodic, suspending the main predication behind a long fronted phrase, while 'it creates opinions, engenders sentiments, suggests the ordinary practices of life' is running, releasing predications in a forward-moving chain.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person 'I' drives the prose with a discoverer's urgency — 'nothing struck me more forcibly,' 'I speedily perceived' — and the tricolon 'creates opinions, engenders sentiments, suggests the ordinary practices of life' has a natural rhetorical crescendo that rewards oral delivery.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'prodigious,' 'tenor,' 'maxims,' 'engenders,' 'empire,' 'terminated.' The register is elevated and ceremonial, consistent with nineteenth-century political philosophy.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in service of its argument, but the rhetorical figures — the parallel 'by giving... by imparting' construction, the tricolon of verbs, the chiastic balance of 'civil society' against 'Government' — draw intermittent attention to the surface as deliberate structural display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real argumentative weight — 'gives,' 'withholds,' 'builds,' 'pays,' 'superintends,' 'lends,' 'receives' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns are also present: 'administration,' 'obligation,' 'performance,' 'existence,' 'instruction.' Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between conceptual abstraction and concrete action.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Hypotactic subordination appears in the conditional chains ('If the State is in need... a town can neither') and relative clauses ('the means by which the townships are compelled'), but the climactic comparative section shifts to paratactic parallel coordination: 'taxes are voted... but they are levied and collected; the existence of a school is obligatory, but the township builds, pays, and superintends it.'
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening conditional sentences are periodic — 'If the State is in need of money, a town can neither give nor withhold' — suspending the main clause behind the condition, but the later comparative sentences run forward immediately: 'Thus, taxes are voted by the State, but they are levied and collected by the township.'
claude_justifications.voice: The prose has performable moments — the parallel antitheses ('the French Government lends its agents to the commune; in America the township is the agent of the Government') invite rhetorical stress and contrast — but the analytical, expository frame keeps it from full oratorical warmth; it is reasoned rather than impassioned.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is neither ceremonially Latinate nor plainly Anglo-Saxon; words like 'administration,' 'obligation,' 'imposts,' and 'uniform system' sit alongside plain terms like 'town,' 'road,' 'schools,' and 'builds.' The register is the unmarked middle of educated analytical prose.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent — it serves its comparative argument without calling attention to itself — but the deliberate antithetical parallelism ('the French Government lends its agents to the commune; in America the township is the agent of the Government') is a self-conscious rhetorical figure that briefly foregrounds the structure of the writing itself.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active first-person verbs drive the argumentative structure — 'I have visited,' 'I met,' 'I found,' 'I have heard' — but the content being argued is carried in nominalizations: 'provincial independence,' 'democratic institutions,' 'utility of provincial liberties,' 'local system.' The verbs belong to the observer; the nouns belong to the subject matter.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage alternates between paratactic parallel constructions ('In America I met... in England I found... I have heard... I have heard') and hypotactic embedding through 'who,' 'which,' 'that,' and 'but.' The parallelism is structural and deliberate, but subordination is present throughout.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and trail qualifications afterward — 'In America I met with men who secretly aspired to destroy...' The one genuinely periodic sentence ('Am I to suppose that when men who are naturally so divided... agree on one point... they are all in error?') stands out precisely because it is exceptional.
claude_justifications.voice: The repeated first-person 'I have visited... I met... I found... I have heard' creates a performable rhetorical rhythm, and the rhetorical question 'Am I to suppose...' invites vocal emphasis and a rising inflection. The closing epigram — 'those who are unacquainted with the institution are the only persons who pass a censure upon it' — has the cadence of a delivered verdict.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'provincial independence,' 'democratic institutions,' 'utility,' 'censure,' 'unacquainted,' 'attribute.' The register is elevated and deliberate, consistent with political-philosophical discourse.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in service of its argument, but the parallel anaphoric structure ('In America... in England,' 'I have heard... I have heard') and the closing chiastic epigram draw mild attention to the surface as rhetorical display — the argument is being performed as well as made.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Abstract nouns dominate the conceptual load — tyranny, interference, arrangements, invasion, temptations, resources, oppression — often chained with prepositional phrases ('in the bosom of,' 'within the grasp of'). Verbs are present but frequently copular or passive ('is established,' 'are to be regulated,' 'are to be governed'), subordinating action to nominal predication.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are consistently embedded through 'because,' 'which,' 'as,' 'for,' and 'and should' constructions, creating ranked hierarchical subordination. The final sentence is a particularly elaborate hypotactic structure with multiple embedded conditionals and causal clauses.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates between periodic and running structures: some sentences front-load qualifying material before the main predication ('This invasion of rights occurs, however, but seldom'), while others deliver the main clause early and trail elaborations ('It supplies the place of those great designs... by a violent or an exasperating interference'). The final long sentence is strongly periodic, suspending resolution through multiple conditional clauses.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries a measured rhetorical authority — the antitheses ('Tastes as well as actions,' 'the families of the citizens as well as the affairs of the State') and the periodic final sentence invite emphatic oral delivery. However, the impersonal third-person construction and abstract subject matter ('it,' 'tyranny') flatten the personal register, preventing full vocal performance.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Consistently Latinate and formal diction throughout: 'established,' 'interference,' 'multitude,' 'arrangements,' 'sovereign,' 'simultaneous.' The register is that of political philosophy — elevated, impersonal, and ceremonial.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its argumentative function, but deliberate rhetorical figures draw some attention to the surface — notably the parallel antitheses ('Tastes as well as actions... families of the citizens as well as the affairs of the State') and the chiastic balancing of 'too weak' and 'too slender' in the final sentence, which signal conscious structural display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real weight — 'comprehends,' 'labors,' 'grows,' 'nurtured,' 'confounded' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns are also prominent: 'attachment,' 'prosperity,' 'influence,' 'welfare,' 'assistance.' Neither mode dominates; the prose moves between conceptual nouns and animating verbs.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The second sentence is a striking paratactic chain — 'it is coeval... it is nurtured... it grows... it is confounded' — coordinated by semicolons in parallel. But the final sentence is hypotactic, embedding relative and 'that' clauses to subordinate the man's awareness and authorization.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Main predications arrive early and qualifications trail behind — 'it is perhaps less generous and less ardent, but it is more fruitful and more lasting' delivers its core assertion immediately. The final sentence opens with its subject and verb ('A man comprehends') before elaborating.
claude_justifications.voice: The parallel antitheses — 'less generous... less ardent, but more fruitful and more lasting' — and the anaphoric 'it is' chain create natural emphatic beats and a rising cadence that rewards oral delivery. The rhetorical architecture is clearly designed for a reader who can stress and perform.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Latinate and formal throughout: 'coeval,' 'nurtured,' 'confounded,' 'authorize,' 'prosperity,' 'rational.' The diction is elevated and abstract, consistent with philosophical-political discourse.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws deliberate attention to its own surface through the anaphoric 'it is' series, the balanced antitheses ('less... less... but more... more'), and the closing chiastic parallelism ('as a portion of his interest... as a portion of his right'). These are conspicuous rhetorical figures, not invisible instruments.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage mixes active verbs with historical force — 'beheaded,' 'pleaded,' 'describes,' 'wrote,' 'undertook,' 'published' — alongside nominal constructions like 'an appeal for Paine's liberation' and 'the state it has since appeared.' Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between narrative action and documentary citation.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The narrative frame is largely paratactic — short declarative sentences coordinated by sequence — but the embedded quotations and the analytical commentary ('For on August 5...,' 'But it is necessary to weigh') introduce hypotactic subordination, creating a layered texture.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and trail qualifications or elaborations afterward — 'He had pleaded for Louis Capet—Kill the king but spare the man.' The one periodic gesture ('But it is necessary to weigh the words just quoted') is exceptional rather than characteristic.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries a distinct rhetorical personality — the dashes, the direct quotations set off with em-dashes, the exclamatory reformulations of Paine's arguments, and the prosecutorial 'But it is necessary to weigh' all invite vocal performance with natural emphases and dynamic range.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is neither bureaucratically Latinate nor plainly Anglo-Saxon — it moves between elevated historical phrasing ('the wrath turned next upon the King of kings') and plain documentary language ('a guard came about three in the morning'). The register is that of educated popular history.
claude_justifications.opacity: The rhetorical parallelism of the two Paine quotations — 'Kill the king but spare the man' / 'Disbelieve in the King of kings, but do not confuse...' — draws deliberate attention to its own structural display, as does the italicized emphasis on 'in the state it has since appeared'; but the documentary sections are transparent, serving the evidentiary argument without surface display.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real argumentative weight — 'collected,' 'managed,' 'added, altered, abridged, dressed them up' — but nominal constructions also appear ('matter altogether of uncertainty,' 'the answer to this question'). Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between action-driven and noun-anchored phrasing.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The passage mixes both modes: hypotactic embedding appears in the long 'whether...or whether' construction and the relative clause chain, while paratactic coordination drives the final list ('added, altered, abridged, or dressed them up') and the sequential narrative of the church mythologists.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most sentences deliver their main predication early and trail qualifications afterward — 'It is, therefore, proper for us to know who told us so, that we may know...' The one exception is the long final sentence, which suspends resolution through the 'whether...or whether' construction, but the overall pattern is running.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is saturated with rhetorical personality — the parenthetical aside '(which, by the bye, is a book of riddles...)' is a direct wink at the reader, and the Socratic question-and-answer structure ('The answer to this question is, that nobody can tell, except that we tell one another so') invites emphatic oral delivery with natural stress and ironic timing.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is deliberately plain and accessible — 'tell one another,' 'dressed them up,' 'by the bye' — with only occasional formal terms ('mythologists,' 'revelation'). This is the register of educated popular argument, not academic or ceremonial prose.
claude_justifications.opacity: The parenthetical aside and the rhetorical question-answer structure draw mild attention to the prose's own argumentative staging, but the dominant impulse is transparency — the language is instrumental, designed to move the reader toward a conclusion rather than to display itself.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry real argumentative force — 'does not prevent,' 'die faster,' 'makes there to be,' 'acquire the habit' — but nominalizations and abstract nouns also appear throughout: 'prevention,' 'longevity,' 'crucifixion,' 'damnation,' 'explanation.' Neither mode dominates; the prose alternates between conceptual noun-clusters and punchy verbal assertions.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The long opening sentence is deeply hypotactic, with nested conditionals, parenthetical elaborations, and 'which/that/because' subordination stacked several levels deep. But the later sentences — 'That it does not prevent our dying is evident, because we all die' and 'They acquire the habit without being aware of the cause' — are comparatively flat and coordinate, creating a rhythm that alternates between embedded complexity and blunt simplicity.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence is strongly periodic, suspending its main predication behind a long conditional apparatus ('must either have meant... or have meant... and consequently... must... apply'). Later sentences flip to running structure, delivering their main claim immediately and trailing qualifications: 'That it does not prevent our dying is evident, because we all die.'
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is saturated with performable contempt — 'these mythologists,' 'That manufacturer of quibbles, St. Paul,' 'a pun or a quibble upon the word death.' There are natural stress points, rhetorical pauses, and a speaker's personality behind every clause; the sarcasm demands vocal delivery.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Latinate theological vocabulary ('damnation,' 'longevity,' 'crucifixion,' 'impertinently,' 'subterfuge') coexists with deliberately colloquial, deflating Anglo-Saxon terms ('pun,' 'quibble,' 'coming off,' 'helped this quibble on'). The mixing is strategic — the low diction is deployed to mock the high.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws conspicuous attention to its own rhetorical surface through the obsessive repetition of 'quibble' (five times), the chiastic formulation 'sins in fact / suffers by proxy; sins by proxy / suffers in fact,' and the theatrical naming of St. Paul as 'that manufacturer of quibbles.' These are deliberate structural and sonic displays, not transparent vehicles for argument.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Nominalizations are present throughout — 'construction,' 'measurement,' 'demonstration,' 'foreknowledge' — but active verbs also carry significant weight: 'man employs,' 'it is called,' 'man speaks,' 'they move.' The anaphoric 'when applied to... it is called' structure keeps verbs visible even as nouns accumulate.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The long central catalogue of 'when applied to X, it is called Y' clauses is strongly paratactic — parallel coordinate units strung in sequence — but the surrounding argument uses hypotactic embedding through 'which,' 'that,' 'or,' and conditional reasoning, creating a mixed structure overall.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentences are periodic, suspending the main point behind conditional and qualifying clauses ('by the aid of which,' 'as eternal and immutable as... or they could not'); but the catalogue section and the closing aphorisms ('It is the soul of science. It is an eternal truth.') are emphatically running.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is built for oral delivery — the anaphoric catalogue ('when applied to... it is called') has a preacher's rhythmic insistence, and the short declarative climax ('It is the soul of science. It is an eternal truth.') demands a pause and a drop in register. Natural emphases and dynamic range are built into the structure.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction mixes Latinate technical terms ('trigonometry,' 'astronomy,' 'demonstration,' 'immutable') with plain Anglo-Saxon constructions ('man cannot invent,' 'the soul of science,' 'drawn by a rule and compass'), producing a middle register aimed at an educated popular audience rather than a specialist one.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws conspicuous attention to its own surface through the sustained anaphoric catalogue ('when applied to... it is called'), the deliberate repetition of 'scientific principles,' 'eternal and immutable,' and 'eclipse,' and the rhetorical climax of the short aphoristic sentences — these are structural displays, not transparent vehicles for content.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage is heavily nominalized — 'the revolution of the earth,' 'the eternal divisibility of matter,' 'the infinity of space,' 'a general knowledge of what was called natural philosophy' — with long prepositional chains accumulating around abstract nouns. The main verbs ('had made,' 'conceived,' 'obtained,' 'began to compare') are sparse anchors in a sea of noun phrases.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The main sentence is a single enormous hypotactic structure in which multiple subordinate 'after' and 'and' clauses are embedded before the main predication arrives; the parenthetical note itself is densely hypotactic, with 'in which' introducing a long relative clause that accumulates parallel noun phrases through repeated 'the revolution of' constructions.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The outer sentence withholds its main clause ('I began to compare... the internal evidence... with the christian system of faith') until after an enormous accumulation of subordinate material — 'After I had made myself master of... and conceived... and obtained' — forcing the reader to hold multiple suspended elements before resolution arrives.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person address ('I proceed,' 'I began to compare') and the direct authorial intrusion of the footnote ('it is for their information I add this note') give the prose a personal, performable quality, but the long enumerative lists within the parenthetical flatten into a recitative drone that resists dynamic vocal range.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is neither ceremonially Latinate nor plainly Anglo-Saxon — terms like 'divisibility,' 'revolution,' and 'magnitudes' sit alongside plain constructions like 'round itself' and 'as they really exist,' producing a practical, instructional middle register characteristic of Enlightenment popular science writing.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose is largely transparent in its aim — it wants to convey information and logical sequence — but the deliberate structural display of the parenthetical note (with its anaphoric repetition of 'the revolution of... the revolution of... the revolution of') draws attention to the surface as a rhetorical enumeration, and the meta-linguistic gesture of the footnote itself foregrounds the author's presence as a self-conscious stylist.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The passage consists entirely of nominal titles — 'The Insufficiency of the Present Confederation to Preserve the Union,' 'The Utility of the Union in Respect to Commercial Relations and a Navy' — built from abstract nouns, gerunds, and prepositional phrase chains with no active verbs or human agents whatsoever.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: The titles are coordinated as a list — a pure paratactic enumeration — with no subordinating conjunctions or embedded clauses; each item stands parallel and independent beside the others.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Most titles are running in that the main noun phrase arrives immediately, but several titles front qualifying prepositional phrases ('In Respect to,' 'From Extent of Territory') that create a mild periodic suspension before the head noun resolves.
claude_justifications.voice: A table of contents is structurally resistant to vocal performance — there is no predication, no argument, no rhetorical arc, and no natural dynamic range; reading it aloud produces only a flat recitation of nominal labels.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The diction is consistently formal and Latinate throughout: 'Insufficiency,' 'Confederation,' 'Dissensions,' 'Insurrection,' 'Restraining the Legislative Authority' — no plain Anglo-Saxon vocabulary appears.
claude_justifications.opacity: The titles function as purely instrumental labels pointing to content beyond themselves; despite the heavy nominal architecture, there is no sound patterning, rhetorical figuration, or self-conscious surface display — the language is entirely referential.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Nominalizations are present (confederacies, attachment, connection, alliance, friendship) but active verbs carry real argumentative weight — 'combine,' 'unite,' 'create,' 'happen,' 'preserving.' The prose moves between noun-heavy analytical claims and verb-driven rhetorical questions and conditionals.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'which,' 'that,' 'as,' 'so,' and 'nor if formed' constructions, creating layered subordination. The logical chain — 'Different commercial concerns must create different interests, and of course different degrees...' — builds through ranked qualification rather than simple coordination.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: Some sentences are periodic, suspending resolution behind conditional and relative material ('An alliance so contrary to their immediate interest would not therefore be easy to form'); others run forward immediately ('The proposed confederacies will be DISTINCT NATIONS'). The passage alternates between the two modes for rhetorical effect.
claude_justifications.voice: The opening rhetorical question, the capitalized emphases (DISTINCT NATIONS, SOUTHERN, NORTHERN), and the rhythmic repetition of 'different' create natural performance cues — rises, stresses, and a prosecutorial cadence that rewards oral delivery.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'confederacies,' 'commodities,' 'political attachment,' 'preserving peace and friendship.' The register is elevated and deliberative, consistent with formal political argument.
claude_justifications.opacity: The deliberate anaphoric repetition of 'different' (six occurrences) and the capitalized proper-noun-style labels (DISTINCT NATIONS, SOUTHERN, NORTHERN) draw attention to the prose surface as a rhetorical device, foregrounding the argument's structure as much as its content.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The prose is dense with nominalizations and abstract nouns — liberty, faction, annihilation, diversity, uniformity, protection, possession, division — chained through prepositional phrases ('from the protection of different and unequal faculties of acquiring property'). Verbs are largely copular or weak ('is,' 'results,' 'ensues'), with the nouns carrying the argumentative weight.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are systematically embedded through 'which,' 'because,' 'as long as,' 'from which,' and 'and from' constructions, creating ranked hierarchical subordination. The analogical structure ('Liberty is to faction what air is to fire') itself requires nested relational embedding.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage alternates strategies: some sentences are periodic, suspending the main predication behind conditional or comparative front-loading ('As long as... different opinions will be formed'), while others are running, delivering the main clause early and trailing elaboration ('Liberty is to faction what air is to fire, an aliment without which it instantly expires').
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries strong rhetorical performance — the analogy ('Liberty is to faction what air is to fire') invites emphatic delivery, and the parallel 'As long as' constructions create a rising cadence that rewards oral stress. The antithetical structures ('worse than the disease,' 'less folly... than it would be') provide natural dynamic contrast.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Formal Latinate diction throughout: 'aliment,' 'expedient,' 'impracticable,' 'annihilation,' 'insuperable,' 'reciprocal,' 'proprietors.' The register is consistently elevated, befitting deliberative political argument.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws sustained attention to its own surface through the extended analogy (liberty:faction::air:fire), the parallel 'As long as' anaphora, and the antithetical chiasmic structures. These rhetorical figures are conspicuous formal displays, not merely instrumental vehicles for content.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The prose is dense with abstract nominalizations and prepositional chains: 'the equilibrium of power,' 'the obligations of good faith,' 'the impulse of any immediate interest or passion,' 'the usual vicissitudes of peace and war, of observance and non-observance.' Verbs are largely copular or passive ('exist,' 'were exhausted,' 'were formed,' 'were broken'), with the conceptual weight carried by noun phrases.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are embedded through 'which,' 'as,' 'from which,' 'how,' and participial constructions, creating multiple levels of subordination. The final long sentence is a showcase of ranked embedding: main clause, relative clause, participial phrase, indirect question, and further relative clauses nested inside each other.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage mixes both tendencies: the opening sentence is running (main predication arrives immediately — 'There is nothing absurd'), while the final sentence is strongly periodic, suspending its evaluative conclusion ('how little dependence is to be placed') behind a long chain of front-loaded context about alliances formed and broken.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose carries rhetorical energy — the antitheses ('scarcely formed before they were broken,' 'observance and non-observance') and the climactic final clause invite emphasis and performance. Yet the impersonal, third-person construction and heavy nominalization suppress a strong individual speaker's presence, placing it between voiced oratory and flat exposition.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Consistently formal and Latinate throughout: 'impracticable,' 'vicissitudes,' 'epidemical,' 'equilibrium,' 'negotiation,' 'contracting powers,' 'sanction.' No Anglo-Saxon plainness intrudes; the diction is uniformly elevated and abstract.

claude_justifications.voice: The prose is richly performable — the catalogues invite rhetorical enumeration, the ironic gravity of 'melancholy object' and 'dear native country' rewards vocal stress, and the mock-solemnity of the final clause ('to have his statue set up for a preserver of the nation') demands a deadpan delivery that makes the satire land.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: Predominantly formal and Latinate — 'importuning,' 'sustenance,' 'deplorable,' 'prodigious,' 'commonwealth,' 'publick' — with the high register functioning ironically, as the elevated diction is applied to beggars, rags, and cabbin-doors.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose draws constant attention to its own surface through ironic incongruity — the gap between the ceremonious register and the squalid subject is itself a rhetorical figure — and through deliberate structural display: the triadic catalogues, the mock-encomium of the final clause, and the sustained persona of the dispassionate projector all foreground the writing as performance.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs with a first-person agent appear throughout ('I propose,' 'I have always found,' 'having turned my thoughts'), but nominalizations and noun-heavy constructions also carry significant weight ('computation,' 'nourishment,' 'occupation,' 'intention'). Neither mode fully dominates.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses are deeply embedded through 'who,' 'which,' 'as,' 'that,' and participial constructions, creating multiple levels of subordination — the final sentence alone suspends its resolution through a long chain of 'instead of... or... or...' before arriving at 'they shall, on the contrary, contribute.'
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The passage repeatedly delays its main predications behind qualifying and conditional material — most strikingly in the final sentence, where the main clause ('they shall contribute') is held back through an elaborate series of negative conditions and participial phrases that must be traversed first.
claude_justifications.voice: The first-person projector's voice is insistently present and performable — the dry precision of 'a solar year,' the clinical 'dropt from its dam,' and the mock-modest 'as to my own part' all create natural emphases and a tone of ironic self-satisfaction that rewards oral delivery.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The prose deliberately mixes registers for satirical effect: formal Latinate diction ('computation,' 'nourishment,' 'raiment,' 'maturely weighed') sits alongside brutally plain Anglo-Saxon terms ('dam,' 'dropt,' 'scraps,' 'begging'), and the collision between the two is the central rhetorical device.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose constantly draws attention to its own surface through the ironic gap between its bureaucratic precision ('exactly at one year old,' 'not above the value of two shillings') and its monstrous content — the language itself is the joke, and the reader cannot look through it to content without noticing the performance of reasonableness.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs carry the ironic argument — 'yield,' 'turn,' 'serve,' 'nursed' — but commercial nominalizations ('commodity,' 'exchange,' 'account,' 'nutriments') are deliberately deployed to reduce children to economic abstractions, which is the satirical point.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'that,' 'which,' 'whether,' and participial constructions, creating the layered subordination of a careful reasoner presenting evidence — the hypotaxis performs the mock-rational voice of the projector.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The first sentence is periodic, suspending its main commercial calculation behind the merchant's assurance and the qualifying age clause; the second sentence runs forward through accumulating coordinate qualifications ('whether stewed, roasted, baked, or boiled') after delivering its shocking predication early.
claude_justifications.voice: The prose is intensely performable — the deadpan accumulation of culinary options ('stewed, roasted, baked, or boiled') and the pivot from commercial to gastronomic register demand vocal control and timing; the irony lives entirely in the gap between the speaker's earnest tone and the content.
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The prose moves between the Latinate commercial register ('saleable commodity,' 'nutriments') and the plain Anglo-Saxon of domestic cookery ('stewed, roasted, baked'), and this tonal collision between high economic discourse and low kitchen vocabulary is the engine of the satire.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose constantly draws attention to its own surface through the deliberate mismatch of registers, the rhetorical figure of the cited authority ('a very knowing American'), and the list of cooking methods that forces the reader to notice the language performing its horror with perfect composure.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: The prose mixes active verbs with practical force — 'reserved,' 'offered,' 'render,' 'dines,' 'seasoned,' 'boiled' — against a scaffolding of administrative nouns: 'consideration,' 'circumstance,' 'entertainment,' 'breed.' The mock-bureaucratic proposal form requires nominal structure, but the culinary specificity keeps verbs alive.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'that,' 'whereof,' 'which,' 'so as to,' and participial qualifications, creating the layered subordination of a formal policy document. The long first sentence stacks three levels of embedded qualification before arriving at its practical conclusion.
claude_justifications.periodicRunning: The opening sentence is periodic — 'that of the hundred and twenty thousand children... twenty thousand may be reserved' — suspending the main clause behind elaborate qualification. But the final sentences shift to running structure, delivering culinary facts immediately and trailing details afterward ('a child will make two dishes... and when the family dines alone').
claude_justifications.voice: The ironic gap between the bureaucratic register and the monstrous content creates enormous performative potential — the voice of the earnest projector can be inhabited and played. Natural emphases fall on the grotesque specifics: 'plump, and fat for a good table,' 'fore or hind quarter,' 'especially in winter.'
claude_justifications.primaryRegister: The prose deliberately collides registers: formal Latinate policy diction ('publick consideration,' 'persons of quality and fortune,' 'circumstance') crashes against plain Anglo-Saxon butchery vocabulary ('boiled,' 'hind quarter,' 'pepper or salt'). The collision is the satirical mechanism.
claude_justifications.opacity: The prose constantly draws attention to its own surface through the sustained ironic persona, the deliberate register collision, and the structural mimicry of projector-pamphlet form. The reader cannot look through to content without noticing the language performing its satirical impersonation — the style is the argument.

claude_justifications.nounVerb: Active verbs with human agents appear throughout — 'computed,' 'reckon,' 'repine,' 'learn,' 'grow,' 'produces' — but these are interspersed with nominal constructions like 'collateral advantage,' 'lessening the number,' 'charge of nursing,' that carry bureaucratic weight. The balance is deliberate: the official-style nominalizations ('prolifick dyet,' 'nutritive meat') are doing satirical work against the active verbs of commerce and appetite.
claude_justifications.parataxisHypotaxis: Clauses embed through 'because,' 'which,' 'when,' 'therefore,' and participial phrases, creating the ranked subordination of reasoned argument — 'because the number of Popish infants, is at least three to one... and therefore it will have one other collateral advantage.' The syntax mimics the logical scaffolding of a policy document.
